newsitem.title: UK: Zinc annual TCs seen lower, lead up - Macquarie.
newsitem.headline: Zinc annual TCs seen lower, lead up - Macquarie.

text.p: Annual treatment charges (TCs) for refining zinc and lead concentrates are likely to deviate, as the opening skirmishes between miners and smelters for 1997 contracts get underway , broker Macquarie Equities Ltd said.
"Lead TCs seem almost certain to rise next year (we think by at least $10 a tonne) as the lead concentrate market appears to be over-supplied," Macquarie said in its weekly report.
But the picture in the zinc talks appears to be different, and a continuation of recent rises in annual terms, which looked like a foregone conclusion nine months ago, is not on the cards now.
Macquarie said that a series of mine accidents, delays and closures have sharply reduced the growth rate in zinc mine output this year.
Also, China has turned from a net exporter to a net concentrate importer this year.
In the Far Eastern spot market there is little material available, and a recent 10,000-tonne parcel destined for China sold at a low $162/tonne cif Japan.

Annual talks are likely to start in earnest in the last week of November in the Far East, with smelters looking for a $7/10 tonne rise in TCs. Miners are looking for $175/180/tonne for TCs, which compares with the 1996 outturn of $190.
Zinc smelters will strongly resist calls for big cuts, citing reduced revenue from by-products such as silver and cadmium.
However, the changed market conditions appear to make a small cut, perhaps $5, inevitable, Macquarie said.
